diagnosis: All four rollouts settled successfully with all three decisive facts (PF1, PF2, PF3) revealed and cited in justification_fact_ids—no disclosure, telepathy, or pacing problems. The gate failed because two content checks are too brittle in their matching. In rollout 0, C7 (gated by PF3) failed because the customer_migration_support commitment detail said "for affected accounts" instead of explicitly restating "42 enterprise accounts," even though the target field and decisions.customer_accounts_supported both contained 42. In rollout 2, C5 (gated by PF1) failed because the engineering commitment detail phrased the scope as "the two remaining endpoint migrations" instead of the exact phrase "remaining two endpoint migrations" used in the three passing rollouts. Both failures are ENCODING MISMATCH: the facts were revealed, cited, and the commitments existed, but the checks' wording thresholds did not accommodate natural paraphrase variation.

C7.why: The support confirmation changes the customer-impact count to exactly 42 accounts and adds the required migration-guide commitment for those accounts.

C5.why: The exact two unfinished endpoints and the backend team's ability to complete them make legacy_csv_exporter the feasible sprint focus and change the scope from an unspecified exporter effort to two endpoint migrations.
